newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ieng Sary makes appearance after two decades.
newsitem.headline: Ieng Sary makes appearance after two decades.

text.p: Hundreds of Khmer Rouge dissidents, mostly women and children, on Monday welcomed scores of reporters flown by helicopter to breakaway leader Ieng Sary's first major public appearance in two decades.

Ieng Sary, foreign minister in the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 rule of terror, initially appeared nervous but gathered himself quickly while explaining his split with former comrade-in-arms Pol Pot, the hardline Khmer Rouge leader.
"Pol Pot has a policy of class struggle, but for me, I have the policy for a nation," said the once highly feared man.

Ieng Sary and his former brother-in-law, Pol Pot, were sentenced to death in absentia for their roles in the deaths of more than one million people from execution, starvation or disease during the brutal rule of the Maoist Khmer Rouge.
At his northwestern Cambodian jungle headquarters, the secretive Ieng Sary discussed his efforts to forge peace with the Phnom Penh government after splitting with the mainstream group last month.

"I would like to inform you that my talks for national reconciliation with the representatives from Phnom Penh were successful," he told more than 100 journalists flown in from Phnom Penh and a Thai border town.
Ieng Sary, wearing a green safari suit, controled the news conference with strict discipline, taking only nine questions from the journalists.
He wrote down all the questions, then answered them one after another through a translator in a mixture of French and Cambodian.
"We want to have a movement to finish war, and our movement is coming from the will of the cadres. Our movement is spreading throughout the country," he said.

Ieng Sary, now in his 60s and formerly seen as the number two to Pol Pot, was quick to distance himself from the hardline leader and the mass genocide in the 1970s, saying he had no power as foreign minister and was not involved in any killings.
Regardless, Ieng Sary showed he still had an iron hand.

Journalists and several dozen Phnom Penh officials, including the deputy defence minister, were required to go through strict security before entering the wooden building where the news conference was held.
Everyone was told to surrender any weapons before entering the hall where Ieng Sary waited.
The atmosphere outside the building was warm, with hundreds of Khmer Rouge dissidents greeting reporters at the helicopters and accompanying them to the press conference site.
His aides handed out propoganda leaflets to the journalists villifying Pol Pot and absolving Ieng Sary.
Former foes became "friends" as Khmer Rouge dissidents pushed aside their armaments and walked arm-in-arm with government troops.

"I am fed up with this old-style uniform and I am just waiting for the day when a new uniform similar to the government ones will arrive," Mitr Sakorn, an officer in the breakaway faction said, while holding an AK rifle in his hand.
The day could be getting closer. Ieng Sary said he had agreed a ceasefire with the Cambodian government, and that contact would begin between their troops and his.
